brief: The Market Ear's bearish NVDA trade (NVDA puts versus AAPL calls, called September 23 when NVDA traded near the top of its range with implied volatility at pre-COVID lows) has "exploded," and weekend allegations against Jensen Huang have added fuel to an already brutal unwind, so the firm is booking profits and closing the trade. NVDA has broken below its 200-day moving average, is approaching a roughly $170 support/trendline cluster, sits at one of its most oversold readings since it was a much smaller stock, and saw realised 5-day volatility hit 100 last week, before the Huang allegations even landed. Credit has caught up: NVDA now underperforms the stress signaled by its own CDS, though CDS spreads themselves stayed calm through November. The stock is down about 26% from its October highs, with multiple compression (now roughly 12-13x FY28E earnings) doing most of the damage rather than any confirmed deterioration in fundamentals; the de-rating reflects AI-capex cyclicality, customer-concentration and financing-cost concerns, which the Huang headlines compound. That cheapened multiple, against an extraordinary growth profile, is why the firm's contrarian instinct is waking up even as it closes its short: the next earnings report is the test, and if demand holds and financing fears ease, it sees significant potential for a violent mean-reversion bounce.
